articles.title: England Women: Ella Toone and Aggie Beever-Jones back for Lionesses as Chloe Kelly and Lauren James miss out through injury
articles.summary: England manager Sarina Wiegman has named a 25-player squad for next month’s World Cup qualifying play-off against Ukraine; Ella Toone and Aggie Beever-Jones return to the squad
articles.body:
Toone was initially excluded from the camp to face Greece in October with Wiegman saying that she had not "played to her potential". She earned a recall following an injury to Lucy Bronze, having impressed with her reaction to the setback.

Chloe Kelly was also a notable absence from the last squad, but this time misses out due to a hamstring problem that has kept her out since the end of September.

Beever-Jones returns having last featured for the Lionesses in their 6-1 victory over Ukraine back in March. She takes the place of Chelsea team-mate Lauren James who is sidelined. Grace Clinton also earns a recall.

Forward Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox are included in the senior squad for the very first time in their careers, while Poppy Pattinson also comes back into the fold.

Goodwin has been in impressive form for the London City Lionesses, scoring three goals in five WSL appearances this season including the equaliser in the 1-1 draw with Arsenal. She will provide competition for Alessia Russo who has suffered from inconsistency this term.

Grace Fisk, Freya Godfrey, Erica Meg Parkinson and Lexi Potter all retain their places after making their debuts in the last camp.

There is also an opportunity for Bronze to make history by becoming just the third woman to reach 150 caps. She currently sits on 148, with injury forcing her to miss the chance in the two-legged tie against Greece.

England are one victory away from booking their ticket to next summer's World Cup in Brazil, with Ukraine standing between them and qualification in the second round of the play-offs.

The Lionesses will face Ukraine away from home in Murcia on Tuesday December 1, before welcoming their opponents to Wembley for the return leg on December 5.

"We know what's at stake in these games and our focus is on producing two strong performances to secure our place at the World Cup," Wiegman said.

"We have worked hard to put ourselves in this position and we now have to finish the job."

The two-match tie will mark England's first outing since head coach Wiegman committed her future to the national team by agreeing a contract extension through to Euro 2029 .

“We are in conversation all the time. The FA are still happy with me and I think they are trailblazers for the women’s game and a great federation to work for," Wiegman said when asked about her extension.

"That’s really important for me of course. Also the connection between the staff and the players and my colleagues in the FA is still very good. There are great challenges too in the nearest future and but also further down the line.

"We have the World Cup coming which takes us back to the Ukraine games that we have to win. Then we have to qualify for the Olympics and then the Euros in Germany."

'Huge talent' Goodwin given chance to excel in England environment

England boss Sarina Wiegman on Isobel Goodwin:

“We always knew that she is a huge talent with high potential. She has shown that over a couple of games, so we want to see her in our environment.

“That [her performance against Arsenal] added to it. Of course we are watching all the time, but I think it helped that she had that great goal and a good performance last Sunday.

"She responded really well and is working really hard. She came into our camp [in October] and was ready straight away. She did her work off camp too and has returned to her club and done very well."

articles.title: Verbruggen, Dumfries... y el 'corrillo de la vergüenza': "Encajamos cinco goles, pero podían haber sido ocho"
articles.standfirst: Los jugadores de Países Bajos se reunieron, a voz en grito, tras encajar el 5-0 ante Alemania
articles.summary: Los jugadores de Países Bajos se reunieron, a voz en grito, tras encajar el 5-0 ante Alemania
articles.body: la derrota ante Alemania (5-0), la peor que ha sufrido Países Bajos en 67 años, dejó una imagen para la historia. Los pupilos de Xavi Hernández formaron un corrillo de 'motu proprio' tras encajar el 5-0 en el 77' para tratar de contener la 'sangría'. Parecía iniciativa de Bart Verbruggen, visiblemente molesto con la desidia de Cody Gakpo nada más encajar el cuarto. El meta del Brighton, que recriminó la actitud de sus compañeros a gritos, negó la mayor. "Tenemos que decirnos la verdad sobre ciertas situaciones, pero no fui yo quien convocó a los jugadores, fue Dumfries", aseguró. "Naturalmente, había enfado entre nosotros. Esto no debería pasar, y uno lo expresa. La rabia y la vergüenza se apoderan de mí", aseguró el lateral del Real Madrid, que ejerció de capitán en ausencia de Virgil van Dijk. "También hubo un intercambio de palabras después del partido [en el vestuario]. Se dijeron algunas cosas con las que estoy totalmente de acuerdo. Principalmente, que los jugadores debemos asumir nuestra responsabilidad cuando las cosas se ponen difíciles. Cuando tenemos problemas como equipo, todo se desmorona", insistía Dumfries. “Tenemos que empezar a mostrar un cambio en nuestro comportamiento, pero no se ve. Tenemos suerte de habernos clasificado ya para cuartos de la Nations League y de tener otra oportunidad en marzo. Como equipo, siento que nos falta algo", confesaba el madridista. Mucho más enfadado, sin duda, estaba Verbruggen: "La forma en la que jugamos fue lamentable. No es la primera vez y esto es inaceptable. Quizás esta vez se notó aún más porque juegas contra un buen rival y te sientes avergonzado, frustrado. Han pasado demasiadas cosas como para señalar el punto exacto, pero esto no tuvo nada que ver con las tácticas ni con la calidad del fútbol, sino de la actitud, algo que no debería pasar. Todos tenemos que darlo todo". El 'número 1' del Brighton iba mucho más allá: "Nunca debería ser una cuestión de actitud. Llevas el León Naranja en el pecho. Todos tenemos que darlo todo, el 100%. En cada partido, hay que cumplir con lo básico: intensidad, energía y compromiso. Eso es lo que nos faltó. Y luego Alemania fue muy superior. Nos marcó cinco goles... pero podrían haber sido ocho. Dejamos de cumplir con nuestras tareas". "Se trataba de demostrar algo de orgullo. Estaba muy claro que ya no íbamos a ganar este partido, pero hay que mostrar un poco de orgullo y asegurarse de que la situación no empeore", aseguró el meta al referirse ya más concretamente al 'corrillo de la vergüenza'. "Estoy frustrado porque no me lo esperaba. Creo que tenemos muy buenos jugadores y un muy buen equipo", subrayaba un abatido Verbruggen. "Es un golpe durísimo. Éste es uno de los peores momentos desde que juego en la selección nacional", confesaba el meta, que no ve la hora de cobrarse 'revancha': "Es una lástima. Hubiéramos preferido permanecer juntos para responder de inmediato, pero no es posible. Ahora todos regresaremos a nuestros clubes". Los de Xavi Hernández deberán esperar al parón de marzo para tener la ocasión de redimirse.

articles.title: Huge boost for Argentina: Scaloni confirms first-choice goalkeeper Martinez will return against Costa Rica just 3 weeks after jaw fracture
articles.summary: Emiliano Martinez returns to Argentina's lineup against Costa Rica just weeks after a serious jaw fracture. Coach Scaloni also plans significant team changes as they adapt without key players like Messi and Di Maria.
articles.body: Emiliano Martinez is ready to return between the posts after several weeks away following a serious jaw injury. The Argentina goalkeeper will start against Costa Rica in Cordoba on Tuesday, with Lionel Scaloni confirming that the 34-year-old has recovered sufficiently to resume playing. His return also gives Argentina an opportunity to assess their options as they begin adjusting to the absence of some of their most influential players.Scaloni confirms Martinez will start after jaw injuryMartinez sustained the injury in October following a collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during Chelsea's 2-0 victory. The impact left the goalkeeper with a fractured jaw, requiring surgery and a period of rehabilitation that kept him out of action for several weeks.He returned to training earlier this month and was included in Scaloni's Argentina squad despite not having played for Chelsea since the incident. The goalkeeper was also pictured working with his international team-mates while wearing a specially made protective mask.Scaloni had considered bringing Martinez back for Argentina's 2-1 defeat to Uruguay on Friday but decided against taking the risk. Instead, Geronimo Rulli started, with Juan Musso and Santiago Beltran also available as alternatives.“Emiliano is going to play in goal, he'll be there,” Scaloni told reporters ahead of Tuesday's friendly.Explaining why he had delayed the goalkeeper's return against Uruguay, the Argentina manager added: “Maybe he was fit for the previous match, but it was a risk, and since we trust Gero (Geronimo Rulli), Juan (Musso) and Santi (Santiago Beltran), we chose to look after him. An extra three days was a prudent choice.”The Costa Rica fixture will therefore mark Martinez's return to action after his recovery, although he will still need to build up his match fitness before resuming regular football at Chelsea.Argentina prepare for changes as Scaloni looks beyond Messi and Di MariaMartinez's return is one of several changes expected as Argentina continue to reshape their team. Scaloni confirmed that he intends to make four or five alterations to the starting line-up against Costa Rica, depending on the final training session.The manager also acknowledged the challenge of moving forward without Lionel Messi and Angel Di Maria, two players who were central to Argentina's recent success. Rather than attempting to find direct replacements, Scaloni wants younger players to develop into important figures within the squad.“We are going to make four or five changes, depending on the final training session to see what works,” he said.“Unlike the first cycle, perhaps now we have more of a foundation and can start filling the gaps left by those great players like Messi and [Angel] Di María who are no longer with us and who are irreplaceable.“We can't truly replace them because they were among the best in the world. However, we can try to fill those gaps with young players who we believe will be with us for a long time. That's the challenge we have-to reach that maximum level, though I don't know when that will be.”Costa Rica friendly offers Martinez a chance to regain match fitnessArgentina will face Costa Rica at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium in Cordoba as they look to respond to Friday's defeat against Uruguay and finish their 2026 campaign with a positive result.For Martinez, the immediate priority will be returning to competitive action without aggravating the injury. The goalkeeper's recovery has allowed him to rejoin the national team, but Tuesday's appearance will also be an important step towards regaining his rhythm before returning to Chelsea.His presence should provide some continuity for Argentina during a period of change, particularly as Scaloni experiments with the players who will be expected to take on greater responsibility in the coming months.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: London City forward Izzy Goodwin receives first England call-up
articles.summary: London City Lionesses forward Izzy Goodwin is named in the England squad for the first time for the World Cup qualifying play-off against Ukraine.
articles.body:
London City Lionesses forward Izzy Goodwin has been named in the England squad for the first time for the World Cup qualifying play-off against Ukraine.

The 23-year-old has been in great form this month and scored in front of England manager Sarina Wiegman at Emirates Stadium on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Arsenal.

"We have always seen her as a huge talent with potential," Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I think London City are developing really well in the games they have showed. She is tall and can head a ball attacking-wise, but also defending.

"She is really quick with her feet and can score goals. I really want to see her in our environment, what she can bring and how close she is to the level that we expect."

There is also a first call-up for goalkeeper Katie Cox, on loan at Nottingham Forest from Chelsea, while Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone returns.

Manchester City duo Niamh Charles and Alex Greenwood, who is injured, are among those to miss out.

The Lionesses play Ukraine in Spain on 1 December before hosting them at Wembley on 5 December. The winner qualifies for next year's Women's World Cup.

"We know what's at stake in these games and our focus is on producing two strong performances to secure our place at the World Cup," said Wiegman.

"We have worked hard to put ourselves in this position and now we have to finish the job.

"Ukraine will provide a challenge and we will prepare with the same focus and determination that we always do."

Chelsea defender Lucy Bronze could make her 150th appearance at Wembley in the second leg.

England travel to Pinatar, Spain a few days before the first leg and opted not to play a friendly match during this extended international break.

"The first part of the block we are [at St George's Park]. We have training sessions and a period of time where we can do some tactical stuff," added Wiegman.

"We also selected more players so that helps us create situations where we can train things and everyone is important. I'm really excited to get ready for these games."

'I'm getting really excited again' - Wiegman's new deal

Wiegman was speaking to media at St George's Park for the first time since signing a new contract that will run until the end of Euro 2029.

It means she could oversee England's fortunes at next year's World Cup if they beat Ukraine, as well as heading up a Team GB squad at the 2028 Olympic Games.

Asked why she wanted to extend her stay, Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Well, first of all the FA is happy with me and I'm really happy with them.

"I'm really grateful for that environment. That is one [reason]. Secondly, I still feel a great connection with staff and players, and of course the country!

"Then we have the challenges ahead. The major tournaments always motivate me. You don't get many moments with the team because it's not like it is at a club.

"In a tournament, you have those moments where you are really together, you can get somewhere with the group and that really excites me.

"Yes, the Olympics would be really great. Next year it's the World Cup, then it's the Olympics, then it's the Euros – that journey ahead really excites me."

Wiegman's contract renewal was kept under wraps and it came as a surprise following their two-legged victory over Greece in October.

The Dutchwoman, who has guided England to successive European titles, said conversations had been ongoing for a while but she had not planned ahead.

"When I signed that first contract in 2020 to join in 2021, it was a four-year contract and I thought, 'ok, this is a long contract, it would be really great if things go well'.

"We all got so excited so I signed another contract until 2027 and now I have until 2029. That is eight years. I never expected that. I also never planned so far ahead.

"I want to feel that I can contribute to the environment and the development of things. I also want that from the other party. You want it to fit and for it to work.

"That decision came over time. At one point you think: 'Yeah, I'm getting really excited again.' That is what you want. To feel the energy, to feel the excitement.

"I still think we have things we can improve. We know the game is improving so quickly so we have to adapt all the time. When you stand still, you are lost."

Wiegman is also determined to improve as a coach and has enjoyed overseeing the development of younger talent as the Lionesses transition.

"It starts with me and about how I am going to develop. I keep learning things about myself too. You need to know yourself really well to do this job," she added.

"The staff and the players will always challenge me in the right ways. It goes back and forth. That is what I want. I really want to improve myself all the time."

articles.title: Almost impossible for Scotland not to qualify... or is it?
articles.summary: BBC Scotland picks its way through the permutations in Scotland's pursuit of Euro 2028 qualification.
articles.body:
"It's almost impossible not to qualify."

The statement is enough to make any Scotland fan uncomfortable, but that's been the relaxed theme going into this Nations League campaign among some outside of Hampden.

Euro 2028 has various different access routes, especially for the host nations of England, Republic of Ireland, Scotland and Wales, who even have two spare spaces between them secured before a ball is kicked.

But, in the bleak, barren and grim aftermath of Scotland's 4-0 scudding by Switzerland in St Gallen, "almost impossible" almost feels like a challenge.

Scotland began with three shots at reaching the finals, where they would play at Hampden Park if they made it. We're now down to two.

They could have qualified for the Euro 2028 finals with help from the Nations League. Not straightforward, but absolutely achievable.

Finish top of group B1 containing Switzerland, Slovenia and North Macedonia, then prevail in the play-off.

In Sebastien Pocognoli's first six games in charge, he failed to deliver that, his new-look squad and system only offering seven points.

Not only that but that third-place finish has further repercussions.

Scotland's next route lies in the Euro qualifiers, with the draw taking place in Belfast on 6 December. Can't wait.

Pocognoli's team will go into pot three for that, making a shot at progression that much more difficult.

That means the Scots could be drawn in a group with the likes of Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, or Austria as their pot 2 opponent.

For example, Scotland could be in a group with Spain, Switzerland, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan. Please, no.

The top 12 group winners and the eight best runners-up go straight through, with the rest of the runners-up going into a play-off with the best Nations League non-qualified group winners.

If Scotland make a hash of that, then do not fear...

Uefa is reserving two spots for the two best-ranked host nations who have not qualified after the completion of the qualifying group stage.

It's now feasible this may come into play.

Going on the assumption England - who have just turned over world champions Spain - will qualify, that leaves Scotland, Wales and Ireland. Despite the qualifying draw being in Belfast, Northern Ireland aren't a host nation.

If one of them qualifies through other means, then happy days.

If they do not, then the Scots will need to hope they are not the lowest-ranked team among the three or they face being locked out of their own house party.

articles.title: Dani Ceballos es duda para el derbi
articles.standfirst: El utrerano realiza trabajo preventivo por unas molestias musculares
articles.summary: El utrerano realiza trabajo preventivo por unas molestias musculares
articles.body: Los jugadores del Betis se han ejercitado esta mañana en la ciudad deportiva Luis del Sol junto a una pancarta que alude al derbi del próximo sábado en el Sánchez-Pizjuán: "Teñir de verde la ciudad", repitiendo una iniciativa de los últimos tiempos antes de El Gran Derbi. La previa está servida desde días antes del partido mientras que los protagonistas se ponen a punto. En el caso del equipo de Manuel Pellegrini, lo ha hecho con dos ausencias: Dani Ceballos y Riquelme. El utrerano tiene unas molestias musculares producidas tras el entrenamiento de ayer y ha realizado trabajo preventivo en el gimnasio. Habrá que estar pendientes a su evolución, pero de momento es duda para el partido frente al Sevilla. Riquelme, por su parte, sufre una faringitis que no le ha permitido entrenar con sus compañeros. La parte positiva es que Pellegrini ha podido contar con Marc Roca y Álvaro Valles, ya de vuelta de su concentración con la Selección. El preparador chileno está pendiente del regreso en los próximos días del resto de los internacionales: Manu González, Ángel Ortiz, Troy Parrott, Ez Abde, Álvaro Fidalgo, Nelson Deossa y Facundo Bernal. La preparación del derbi está siendo atípica en ambos lados por la ausencia de jugadores, en el caso del Betis, con mayor participación en este parón de selecciones. Otra nota favorable para los intereses verdiblancos es que Cucho Hernández suma una nueva sesión. El cafetero va aumentando las cargas de trabajo y ha estado de manera parcial con el grupo. Todavía quedan unos días por delante, pero el delantero podría, al menos, entrar en la citación para el primer derbi de la presente temporada.

articles.title: Premier League: Growing amount of players out to emulate David Beckham
articles.summary: Why Premier League players are trying their luck on goal from long range more regularly.
articles.body:
David Beckham's goal from the halfway line against Wimbledon in 1996 is one of football's iconic moments.

It helped to catapult the Manchester United midfielder to global stardom and remains a staple of highlight reels.

The impudence to shoot from such a distance highlighted the exceptional talent and character of the future England captain.

Premier League players are now trying their luck from long range more regularly, testing their instinct, precision and technique.

Diego Gomez's stunning 51-metre (56-yard) strike for Brighton against Crystal Palace last month added to the spectacular list in the Premier League, while players in the EFL and FA Cup have contributed their own.

There have already been 19 attempts from over 50 metres this season, on course to beat last season's Premier League total of 26.

Of the 2,733 shots in the Premier League this term, 0.7% of them have come from over halfway - up on 0.3% over the course of last season.

This sample size is admittedly small. And in the case of goals scored from distance lower down the football pyramid, this is data that isn't readily available.

But why are we seeing a growing number of shots being taken from such extravagant distance?

Gomez tried to score from deep in his own half during Brighton 's 2-0 win at Sunderland on 10 October.

A week later, he beat Walter Benitez with the longest-range goal in the Premier League since Wayne Rooney's 57.6m strike for Everton against West Ham in 2017.

The Paraguayan took advice from Lionel Messi, when the pair were at Inter Miami, to always look to play the ball forward to another level.

It is not just Premier League players who are trying their luck from outrageous distances.

Charlie McNeill scored from halfway for Crewe in their recent 2-1 FA Cup win against AFC Wimbledon.

The on-loan Sheffield Wednesday forward, who played once for Manchester United before leaving Old Trafford in 2024, beat goalkeeper Joe Bursik to open the scoring.

Having done it while at Manchester City and Manchester United 's academies, the 23-year-old felt his latest attempt was instinctive.

He told BBC Sport: "Goalies nowadays are always quite high up the pitch - playing a sweeper-keeper role - and I always have a thought if I ever got into that situation to have a go.

"You see it more and more. I had the opportunity so I thought: 'Why not have a go?'

"It was one of those goals. I turned and saw him off his line and in that split-second made the decision to shoot.

"I knew I caught it sweetly and I was following it the whole way in so I knew it had a good chance, but as the keeper was going back I thought he was going to get it.

"When I watched it back it dropped quite early, but as it was getting closer and closer I thought it was going to go over because it went quite high but it dropped in."

McNeill joins a growing number of players to have scored from the halfway line or inside their own half over the past 18 months.

Preston Fearon, now on loan at Forest Green, scored two goals from around the halfway line for West Ham Under-21s in their win against Burnley last month.

Gbemi Arubi was barely a stride over the halfway line when he scored for Burton against Peterborough in October.

Last season, Abdul Fatawu (Leicester), Ryan Ledson (Huddersfield), Reyes Cleary (Barnsley), Regan Hendry (Mansfield) and Sammy Braybrooke (Newport) all scored from the halfway line or inside their own half in the EFL.

So what is sparking this apparent trend?

Is it all about the goalkeeper's position, as they stand higher up the pitch to either stop opposition attacks or get their own team moving?

"You've got to execute it properly, but it plays a big part. Most keepers are like that, high out the net, because we are playing over the top so they are there first, to get the ball," said McNeill.

"I have always had it in my head and have tried it a couple of times. Although it's not like I do my homework and see he is always off his line. It's one of those instinctive moments."

Asmir Begovic holds the record for the longest-range Premier League goal when the goalkeeper scored from 95.7m for Stoke against Southampton in 2013.

Two other goalkeepers have scored from their own half: Tim Howard for Everton against Bolton in 2012 and Paul Robinson, who netted for Tottenham against Watford in 2007.

Yet they were flukes rather than by design - similar to Barrow goalkeeper Ben Winterbottom's goal from his own half in their 3-0 National League win at Gateshead on Saturday.

Robinson, who also scored for Leeds against Swindon in 2004 , external , feels conceding from distance is now a risk managers are willing to take.

The former England international said: "We've seen the game evolve in the way where the goalkeeper becomes a key figure in starting a pattern of play. The manager wants the goalkeeper at the base of the back three, four or five.

"But then also we're seeing a lot more teams playing with a higher line and the goalkeeper then has to take a higher line of starting position to read the through ball.

"When your team are playing a high line, you obviously have to be further up the field and you're concentrating on where your defensive line is, as opposed to where the football is at times.

"It's one of those things modern-day managers are willing to accept if and when it does happen, because of the way they want their goalkeeper to play.

"We see so many managers come out now and say: 'It's OK. I'm quite happy with them making mistakes. This is the way I want them to play. Blame me because that's what I've asked them to do.'

"We're probably entering that type of territory with it."

With attackers aware of the higher starting position of opposing keepers - a result of teams pressing high - and likely to have been encouraged by the success of other long-range efforts across football, attempts from extreme distance are becoming more frequent in the Premier League this season.

The conversion of efforts from more than 50 metres have increased too - up to 5.3% this season, compared to 1.1% across the previous three seasons combined, with Gomez's strike the first Premier League goal scored from over 50 metres since the 2023-24 season.

It's a small sample size, so more time is required for clearer trends, at least in the Premier League to be established.

But with more long shots being taken and keepers starting higher, there is a suggestion (and hope) we may see more Goal of the Season contenders before the term is out.

articles.title: Vuelve el mejor Vini
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Real Madrid anotó su primer 'hat-trick' con Brasil y su quinto gol en apenas dos partidos tras los dos metidos a Japón
articles.summary: El delantero del Real Madrid anotó su primer 'hat-trick' con Brasil y su quinto gol en apenas dos partidos tras los dos metidos a Japón
articles.body: Brasil se dio un festín ante Singapur para resarcirse de la derrota del pasado sábado ante Japón. Vini volvió a ser el mejor, esta vez con un sensacional 'hat-trick' en apenas 12 minutos de partido. Endrick también quiso unirse a una fiesta a la que también se apuntaron Estevao, Rayan y Allan, que logró el séptimo aunque con ayuda de Suhaimi. Los de Ancelotti vuelven sin lesiones y con una goleada que maquilla la imagen dada en los partidos anteriores. Brasil necesitaba una victoria así para resarcirse de la dura derrota ante Japón el pasado sábado. Allí, también en Singapur, Vini mostró su mejor versión, pero ante los locales terminó de explotar. El madridista no tenía tiempo que perder antes de volver a Madrid y ya en el minuto ocho estrelló un balón contra la madera. La segunda vez no falló. Un gran recorte en el área para acomodarse el disparo a su zurda sirvió para abrir festival brasileño. Sólo seis minutos después llegó el doblete. Contra de los de Ancelotti comandada por Endrick, que quiso ser generoso y asistió a su izquierda, donde venía Vini como un misil para anotar casi a placer. Pero del delantero quería más, y nuevamente seis minutos después, el tercero. Una buena jugada de Estevao por banda derecha regaló al madridista el 'hat-trick' teniendo sólo que empujarla. Tres goles en 12 minutos. Locura en Brasil, que celebraba así el primer triplete de Vini con la camiseta de su país. El carnaval goleador no terminó ahí. Endrick quiso unirse a la fiesta con un sensacional disparo raso desde fuera del área que hacía el cuarto del encuentro antes del descanso, donde pudieron ser cinco si no hubieran anulado el de Estevao por falta de Vini al portero Mahbud. El pistón no bajó en la segunda parte. Estevao hizo el quinto al poco de la reanudación, anularon un gol por fuera de juego a Vini y Rayan estrelló un balón contra la madera en cuestión de diez minutos. Una apisonadora brasileña que nunca tuvo piedad de los singapurenses. Con todo bajo control, era momento de dar descanso. Ancelotti no quería correr riesgos de una posible lesión y decidió quitar a Vini, que jugó una hora de partido. El madridista pareció no estar del todo conforme y querer seguir en el campo, pero no había necesidad. Rayan hizo el sexto y un centro de Allan hizo que Suhaimi se la colara en propia puerta, lo que le faltaba a los singapurenses. Así terminó un encuentro que sirvió para limpiar la imagen de Brasil, cuyos jugadores volverán a sus respectivos clubes sanos y salvos. Y, en el caso de Vini, con una sonrisa en la cara después de haber recuperado su mejor versión.

articles.summary: One week of chaos is liable to change our perceptions, but the 2026 Heisman Trophy is probably down to three candidates.
articles.body:
One week of chaos is liable to change our perceptions, but the 2026 Heisman Trophy is probably down to three candidates.

Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith have dominated the discussion for most of the campaign. They are practically locks for a trip to New York as top-four finishers and Heisman finalists.

The main challenger right now is Devon Dampier. He's on the verge of leading Utah to an unbeaten regular season.

But how many votes will Notre Dame's CJ Carr or Georgia's Gunner Stockton steal?

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+12500)

Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana : Although the Hoosiers have plenty of uncertainty on offense, Becker has remained a steady force. He's racked up 53 catches for 950 yards and 10 touchdowns—the latter two of which are top-10 marks nationally.

Malachi Toney, WR, Miami : Toney will miss the rest of the regular season due to an ankle injury. Nevertheless, he's amassed 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and is third in the country with 13 scores for a respected Miami team.

Jesse Legree, WR, Oregon State : Three straight losses have doomed any hopes of Legree sticking in the Heisman race. Oregon State is 5-5, and team success historically has mattered to voters. Still, the star freshman has pulled in 73 passes for FBS-high marks of 1,349 yards and 15 touchdowns.

LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina : Unfortunately for Sellers, an ankle injury sidelined him in last week's loss to Arkansas. But there may be a little support after Sellers propelled the Gamecocks' second-half surge. He's thrown for 2,100 yards, rushed for 637 and totaled 24 touchdowns this season.

Arch Manning, QB, Texas : It's been ugly at times—borderline bad on occasion. Despite it all, Manning has Texas on the brink of the College Football Playoff. He absolutely won't win the Heisman, but Manning will probably have a few supporters if the Horns topple Arkansas and Texas A&M to finish 10-2.

Keelon Russell, QB, Alabama : A first-year starter, Russell has navigated a tough schedule and kept Alabama on a CFP track. Since he doesn't have a true signature game, Russell likely won't be a finalist—let alone win this award. If the Crimson Tide close the regular season 10-2, Russell will factor into the voting.

Nate Sheppard, RB, Duke : The bad news is Duke fell at Miami, keeping the spotlight off Sheppard. But he collected 224 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, raising his season totals to FBS-leading marks of 1,719 yards and 23 scores. Sheppard is a locked-in All-American who merits a bit of Heisman love.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : After a blowout loss against Texas Tech, Mestemaker is a candidate to fade. Oklahoma State's 6-4 record is not helping his case. However, the combination of leading the FBS in both passing yards (3,239) and touchdowns (30) while elevating a program that was a disaster last season could be compelling to some.

DeSean Bishop, RB, Tennessee : An upcoming clash with LSU is Bishop's final opportunity to bolster his profile. So far, he's rushed for 1,163 yards and 13 touchdowns. If the Vols knock out LSU, they'll be 9-2 and positioned to make the CFP with a final victory over rival Vanderbilt.

Gio Lopez, QB, Wake Forest : Since the start of September, Wake Forest has notched six straight wins by 24-plus points—five with margins of 34 or more. Wake's overall excellence comes down to Lopez, who has passed for 2,377 yards and 19 touchdowns to a single interception and has scampered for 351 yards with eight more scores.

Georgia seems to be the most complete team in the country, as Gunner Stockton should benefit from the Dawgs' recent tear.

Most notably, the veteran QB had a five-touchdown day at Ole Miss two weeks ago. He followed up that performance with 258 total yards and two touchdowns in Saturday's rout of Missouri.

Stockton is unlikely to hoist the Heisman. While this production is nice and efficient, his 2,348 offensive yards and 24 scores are more good than great.

But if someone above him slips, Stockton could head to New York as a finalist.

The essential part is that UGA keeps winning. The Dawgs will be heavy favorites against both South Carolina and Georgia Tech.

Notre Dame also has a great QB leading a well-rounded roster.

CJ Carr has guided the Fighting Irish to a 9-1 record, which includes a marquee win over Miami. He passed for 319 yards and three touchdowns in a 31-24 triumph that bolstered ND's postseason résumé.

As with Stockton, though, Carr doesn't quite have the case of a Heisman winner. The numbers—2,385 passing yards and 26 total touchdowns to three interceptions—are excellent yet not overwhelming.

Don't mistake that for criticism; he's a terrific QB on a fantastic team.

Carr's path to commanding a greater share of votes is a pair of flashy stat lines against SMU and Syracuse to close the season 11-1. Any stumbles from the players above him would help, too.

From an impact and production standpoint, Dampier is well beyond that label. He's passed for 2,257 yards and 22 touchdowns to eight picks. He's also run for 582 yards and nine scores with a 29-yard reception. Utah is a perfect 10-0.

Specific to the Heisman, though, he's the easiest to omit on three-player ballots. Right or wrong, the star power of Smith and Mensah will attract votes.

Dampier has also been terrific in key games, leading the Utes to Top 25 victories over Houston, BYU and Arizona. He rushed for two touchdowns in each contest and threw for four combined passing scores.

In short, he's done just about everything expected of a worthy Heisman winner.

Should the Utes finish 13-0 with a Big 12 title, Dampier will have an awfully compelling case to leap Smith and/or Mensah.

Julian Sayin's elbow injury has basically ruined the Buckeyes' postseason hopes. Recent setbacks to USC and Oregon sent OSU to a dreaded third loss.

Even without him, though, Jeremiah Smith has continued to excel.

Whether that would happen as Luke Fahey stepped in was a fair question, given the 20 games of chemistry between Sayin and Smith. Fahey, a true freshman, had played zero significant snaps at this level.

The answer is 28 receptions, 333 yards and three touchdowns in three games. Smith has climbed to 80 catches for 1,317 yards and 15 scores overall.

Best player in the country. Absolutely. Heisman? He may narrowly miss.

Since the Buckeyes likely won't reach the Big Ten Championship Game, Smith needs to stuff the stat sheet opposite Nebraska and rival Michigan.

Thanks to a win over Duke and Wake Forest's rout of SMU, Miami has nearly clinched a place in the ACC Championship Game. That'll be official if the 'Canes beat either Virginia Tech or Boston College over the next two weeks.

That 13th contest may be a Heisman-level difference for Darian Mensah.

So far, he leads the FBS in completion rate (76.3) and holds top-five marks in passing yards (3,076; fifth), yards per attempt (9.7; third) and touchdowns (29; tied for second) with two interceptions. He's also rushed for 144 yards and two scores.

Losing to Va Tech or BC would be crushing. Miami will be a big favorite in both games, as QBs often bear the brunt of criticism in an upset.

Mensah, however, has an obvious path to a résumé with elite production and immense team success. Three more victories would have Mensah lifting the hardware of an ACC title. It might not be the only trophy he raises.

articles.title: El Valencia inicia la 'mudanza' al Nou Mestalla
articles.standfirst: Arranca la venta de localidades con el socio número 1 a la cabeza
articles.summary: Arranca la venta de localidades con el socio número 1 a la cabeza
articles.body: Primer día del traslado. Llegó la hora de la mudanza. Durante el día de hoy se ha activado la venta de localidades para el Nou Mestalla con la simbólica presencia del socio número 1, José Benet, que ha sido el primero en poder elegir entre las más de 70.000 localidades que ofrece el nuevo coliseo valencianista. Desde hoy y durante los próximos meses, los socios que se han ido agrupando irán pasando por las instalaciones habilitadas por el club para reservar sus localidades de cara al estreno del nuevo estadio durante la próxima temporada. El club irá publicando día tras días las localidades que quedan libres para que el proceso se agilice a la hora de elegir zonas cuando las opciones vayan menguando debido a la venta. Entre los primeros en elegir se encuentran las personas con movilidad reducida que tienen zonas habilitadas para ellos pero que pueden elegir sus preferidas. Esta fase que arranca hoy tendrá su final a finales de abril o principios de mayo cuando todas las reservas hayan sido atendidas. El proceso va a ser largo, porque tienen que pasar por las instalaciones situadas en los bajos del viejo Mestalla, en la sala 1923, los miles de 'capitanes' de los grupos creados para las reservas y elegir las localidades deseadas dentro de las que queden disponibles hasta cubrir las más de 50.000 reservas que ya se han activado. Hay que recordar que en esta fase el socio no desembolsa dinero alguno y el pago se realizará ya en la campaña de abonos del próximo verano.

articles.title: El Andorra no recurrirá la sanción de 12 partidos a Owono
articles.standfirst: El director general del club, Jaume Nogués, defiende que el portero merece volver a jugar y pide que no se le culpabilice de la tragedia
articles.summary: El director general del club, Jaume Nogués, defiende que el portero merece volver a jugar y pide que no se le culpabilice de la tragedia
articles.body: El Andorra no presentará ningún recurso contra la sanción de 12 partidos impuesta a Jesús Owono por el choque con Jesús de Miguel, que acabó con el fallecimiento del jugador del Tenerife al día siguiente. Así lo ha confirmado este martes el director general de la entidad tricolor, Jaume Nogués, durante una entrevista en el programa 'Avui serà un bon dia' de Ràdio i Televisió d'Andorra, en la que ha asegurado que el propio guardameta tampoco contempla esta posibilidad. "Jesús tampoco lo ve", ha explicado, apuntando que recurrir "socialmente no estaría bien visto". Pese a ello, el dirigente ha cuestionado la resolución del Comité de Disciplina de la RFEF, cuya redacción considera que "no está bien hecha", así como el momento en el que fue comunicada, el pasado viernes, cuando el equipo viajaba hacia Almería. En este sentido, Nogués ha defendido que Owono merece tener la oportunidad de volver a jugar al fútbol y ha insistido en que no se le puede responsabilizar del trágico desenlace. "Se lo merece porque es lo que más le gusta, es su profesión", ha manifestado, aunque ha reconocido que regresar a los terrenos de juego será especialmente complicado y que la decisión dependerá exclusivamente del futbolista. Asimismo, ha subrayado que la recuperación emocional del portero irá mucho más allá de los encuentros de suspensión y ha pedido que no se le señale como culpable de lo ocurrido: "No hagamos una segunda víctima de todo esto. No hagamos que Jesús sea el culpable". Respecto a su estado anímico, el director general ha explicado que Owono quedó profundamente afectado tras el accidente y que se encontraba en estado de shock cuando representantes del club acudieron a visitarlo a su domicilio. Desde entonces, el Andorra ha tratado de acompañarlo y considera necesario que cuente con ayuda profesional para afrontar su recuperación. "Nosotros lo que tenemos que hacer es acompañarlo, ser muy empáticos y estar a su lado", ha señalado Nogués, quien también ha lamentado las críticas recibidas por el guardameta de personas que no lo conocen. Además, ha confirmado que el exportero del Alavés tiene intención de contactar con la familia de Jesús de Miguel para trasladarle personalmente sus condolencias, como ya avanzó MARCA. Por último, Nogués ha recordado los momentos de desconcierto y angustia que se vivieron en el vestuario del Andorra después del choque, una situación que ha calificado de "drama absoluto". El dirigente ha reconocido que inicialmente no eran conscientes de la gravedad de lo sucedido, pero que la reacción de los futbolistas les hizo comprender la magnitud de los hechos. En este contexto, ha defendido que el club intentó actuar "de la manera más humana posible", priorizando el acompañamiento a la familia y al Tenerife, antes de reiterar que considera la acción un accidente marcado por una terrible mala suerte y que debe analizarse teniendo en cuenta todo el contexto de la jugada.

articles.title: El Barça no tiene ninguna oferta por Balde
articles.standfirst: Juventus, PSG y Mónaco se han interesado por él
articles.summary: Juventus, PSG y Mónaco se han interesado por él
articles.body: El Barcelona tiene muy claro que una de las claves para poder fichar a un central, actualmente la prioridad de mercado para Hansi Flick, es gestionar la salida de Balde. De esta manera, el club azulgrana dispondría de un mayor margen de 'Fair Play' financiero para poder incorporar a un central de primer nivel, ya que en estos momentos su capacidad es mínima después de los fichajes realizados el pasado verano. En los últimos días están apareciendo rumores sobre numerosos equipos que estarían interesados en hacerse con sus servicios. En el Barcelona, sin embargo, son muy cautos, porque el pasado verano también se habló de varios clubes interesados en el lateral y, a la hora de la verdad, no llegó ninguna oferta importante que permitiera su salida. En estos momentos, y a pesar de todos estos rumores, la realidad es que el club azulgrana no ha recibido ninguna oferta de ningún equipo. Saben que Jorge Mendes se está moviendo en busca de un destino para su jugador, pero, más allá de esta situación, no tienen más información. El club azulgrana está a la espera de que el agente portugués les comunique alguna novedad, aunque todavía es pronto para dar ningún paso. El último club que se ha interesado por Balde ha sido la Juventus. La opción que plantea el conjunto italiano sería una cesión y no un traspaso, ya que el precio de este último sería muy elevado: rondaría los 40 millones de euros. La Juve pretende conseguir una cesión hasta final de temporada sin ninguna opción de compra, según publica el Corriere dello Sport, porque tiene puestas sus miras en David Raum, lateral del Leipzig al que querría fichar en verano. Por este motivo, la Juve no quiere comprar a Balde. No es el único club interesado. El Manchester United también se ha fijado en el lateral, y no es algo nuevo, porque el pasado verano ya quiso ficharlo. El problema fue que, cuando se abrió la puerta de salida de Balde, el club inglés ya había realizado varios fichajes y no tenía dinero para más incorporaciones. La única posibilidad era una cesión, pero Balde no estaba de acuerdo. Otros dos clubes que también estarían detrás del jugador son el PSG y el Mónaco. Sin embargo, ninguno ha movido ficha al respecto por el momento. De momento, todo son rumores. El mercado se abre el 1 de enero y todavía hay tiempo para ver qué opciones se presentan. Se ha especulado con que Jorge Mendes podría viajar a Barcelona próximamente para conocer la situación de Balde y presentarle las opciones que tiene de cara a una posible salida en invierno. Lo que está claro es que el lateral tiene pocas opciones de jugar en el Barcelona. Flick se lo ha demostrado claramente al dar prioridad a otros futbolistas, como Espart, Cancelo e incluso Gerard Martín, tal y como sucedió en el último partido.

articles.title: Diallo Wants to Restore "Broken" Trust in Soccer as He Challenges Infantino for FIFA Presidency
articles.summary: PARIS (AP) — French soccer leader Philippe Diallo wants to restore "broken" trust in the sport's governance and rid the game of the "poison of division" after confirming his intention on Tuesday to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency.
articles.body:
PARIS (AP) — French soccer leader Philippe Diallo wants to restore "broken" trust in the sport's governance and rid the game of the "poison of division" after confirming his intention on Tuesday to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency.

His candidacy was ratified following an executive committee meeting at the French soccer federation's headquarters in Paris.

"A few days ago, my colleagues from the UEFA Executive Committee asked me if I could carry this voice in the world of football," Diallo, 63, said. "I wasn't initially a candidate, but the insistence of my European colleagues led me to accept the offer to be the candidate for the FIFA presidency."

UEFA is pursuing legal action in U.S. courts and seeks discovery of evidence for a possible criminal complaint against Infantino in his and FIFA's home country Switzerland alleging financial mismanagement.

FIFA accused UEFA of a "smear campaign" against its president in a court filing in Colorado.

Concerns include Infantino seeming to act alone in creating a peace prize for U.S. President Donald Trump last year and, at the World Cup, letting United States forward Folarin Balogun avoid a mandatory ban for a red card after Trump intervened .

"Since a few months there have been a series of decisions taken inside FIFA: I think of the peace prize, I think of the distribution of revenue of television rights in the United States, the red card for Balogun, the length of the halftime break in the final and the private investors (sell-off plan)," Diallo said.

"All of these decisions shocked the world of football in a very big way, the fans, the clubs, the sponsors, the federations."

Diallo said "there are a lot of questions" for Infantino and that the turmoil and fall-out has seriously damaged the game.

"It created a situation this summer whereby the trust placed in FIFA and it's president was broken," he said. "They have damaged the image of football and have introduced the poison of division."

UEFA, European soccer's ruling body, proposed Diallo on Monday after a meeting of its 21-member executive committee that includes the French Football Federation president.

"It was important that another voice can carry another vision, more respectful toward what we love in football," Diallo added on Tuesday. "I could not shy away from the demands. I think I have the experience, the convictions and the values which offer a credible alternative.

"I think with my candidature comes hope of a change. It is support of my European colleagues and my executive committee which allows me to say this. Football deserves a credible change which I represent. I am candidate for the FIFA presidency. What happened in recent months was shocking."

Diallo sat smiling alongside Zinedine Zidane when he was announced as France's new national team coach in late July.

Diallo is a long-time soccer administrator with French clubs, and the league, who rose to interim president at the FFF in January 2023, before being fast-tracked in an election of UEFA member federations to join the European body's executive committee.

Diallo has worked for world soccer's ruling body FIFA as a judge on its Dispute Resolution Chamber, handling contract disputes between players and clubs.

Until his emergence, speculation on a candidate focused on Qatari soccer and broadcast executive Nasser Al-Khelaïf i , the president of Champions League titleholder Paris Saint-Germain and a UEFA executive committee member. He said he would not run against Infantino, who has backing from Qatar .

Focus them shifted onto former Arsenal coach Arsène Wenger, hired by FIFA since 2019 as the global head of developing the game. He made it clear he would not stand.

When the World Cup ended on July 19, Infantino was set to be re-elected unopposed effectively by a coronation. FIFA said he had about 200 letters of support from the 211 member federations who will vote in March in Rabat, Morocco.

But Diallo formally withdrew the FFF in September, citing that trust in Infantino was broken by the World Cup sell-off plan secretly devised with Joshua Kushner, the younger brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

"The last time I saw him (Infantino) was at the World Cup, he came to a few France games. I have known him for a long time," Diallo said. "I regret, as others did, that he did not share the ideas of his projects ... it was an unacceptable act of defiance."

Diallo said the 48-team men's 2026 World Cup generated record profits of $15-16 million, vastly more than the 2022 edition of 32 teams in Qatar. Therefore the sell-off plan, which "no one really understands", was totally baffling.

"FIFA's (cash) reserves are $5-6 million," Diallo said. "We find it hard to understand ... the need to find private investors to bring further billions, when these billions are already here."

Infantino has promised at least $25 million in development funds to each member federation through 2030.

"On the basis of (cash) reserves that had lay dormant for years and would still be dormant in FIFA accounts if we had not intervened," Diallo said. "There are a lot of things that need answering, there is no clarity regarding this and there are curious strategies."

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp said he'd welcome a new FIFA president and that Infantino has turned out worse than Blatter.

"To beat him I need 106 votes, the absolute majority," said Diallo, who will announce his campaign team in Belfast in early December. "I will have a clear program of solidarity and excellence, and guarantee those who love soccer that these values will be respected."

He can count on the support, too, of French President Emmanuel Macron.

"The President supports my candidature," he said, adding that he has been "pleasantly surprised" by the number of people from the African and Asian soccer federations who have offered him their support since his candidacy became known.

articles.title: Real Madrid: Man convicted for racist abuse of Kylian Mbappe
articles.summary: A man has been convicted of a hate crime after directing racist insults at Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe during a La Liga match at Real Oviedo in 2025.
articles.body:
A man has been convicted of a hate crime after directing racist insults at Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe during a La Liga match at Real Oviedo in 2025.

A court in Asturias, the northern Spanish region where Oviedo is based, handed down a guilty verdict against the man for the abuse at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium.

The defendant was sentenced to 11 months in prison, alongside a fine and a number of additional disqualifications.

The prison sentence has been suspended on the condition that he does not enter any stadium hosting official sporting competitions for a period of two years.

The ruling represents another legal development in Spanish football's ongoing battle against racism, with Real Madrid continuing to pursue criminal action against individuals responsible for discriminatory abuse directed at the club's players.

The club highlighted the latest conviction follows previous successful legal cases involving racist insults aimed at Vinicius Jr at Valencia's Mestalla , Mallorca's Son Moix, Rayo Vallecano's Vallecas and Real Valladolid's Jose Zorrilla stadiums.

Real Madrid acted as a private prosecutor in the Asturias case and says the club will continue to take legal action in other incidents involving racist behaviour.

"Real Madrid reaffirms its commitment to combating racism and eradicating any racist behavior in football and sports," a club statement said.

It comes after Spain's head coach Luis de la Fuente insisted there was no racism in Spain or in Spanish football before their Nations League meeting with England in Madrid on Sunday.

De la Fuente was asked whether the fact Thomas Tuchel had said he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the match showed that more work needed to be done to tackle racism in Spanish football.

But he responded: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism.

"Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us."

The Spanish Football Federation was fined last month and ordered to partially close a stadium after supporters directed Islamophobic and xenophobic chants towards Muslims during a match against Egypt in Barcelona.

articles.title: Ugly scenes against India! Palestine player thows kicks, makes alleged racist gesture - Watch
articles.summary: India's Under-17 team secured a convincing 4-1 victory over Palestine in their AFC U17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
articles.body: India's Under-17 team secured a convincing 4-1 victory over Palestine in their AFC U17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday. However, the match attracted attention for reasons beyond football, with an early red card, a controversial gesture that raised accusations of racism, and a temporary suspension due to heavy rain.India and Palestine entered the contest with six points each from their opening two matches. India got off to a flying start in the eighth minute when Kamgouhao Doungel scored after Hrishikesh Manavathi capitalised on an error by Palestine's Mohammed Jamhour.Just two minutes later, Jamhour was sent off for kicking Raj Wahengbam and standing on his arm, leaving Palestine with ten players.Despite being a player down, Palestine fought back and equalised in the 33rd minute through Yazan Khalifah's penalty after Abdelrahman Sharifeh was brought down inside the box.However, another incident involving India's captain and Palestine's number 19 soon attracted widespread attention. The Palestinian player reportedly made a gesture suggesting that the Indian captain smelled bad.The action drew criticism because it echoed a hurtful stereotype targeting people from India and South Asia.The match also faced interruptions due to heavy rain in Kuala Lumpur, forcing a temporary suspension at the start of the second half.India seal a comfortable victoryAfter play resumed, India took control of the contest. Mukundo Singh restored India's lead in the 52nd minute with a powerful strike from outside the box. Eight minutes later, Dallalmuon Gangte extended the advantage by converting Mukundo's cut-back.India completed the 4-1 victory in the 89th minute when Zoramdinthara Lalhunmawia headed home Mukundo's corner.The win marked India's third consecutive victory in Group E and brought them closer to qualifying for the AFC U17 Asian Cup Uzbekistan 2027. articles.title: Fan who racially abused Kylian Mbappe at LaLiga match avoids prison time
articles.summary: The fan abused Mbappe during Real Madrid’s win at Real Oviedo in August 2025
articles.body:
A fan who racially abused Kylian Mbappe during a LaLiga match last year has been handed an 11-month suspended prison sentence after being convicted of a hate crime.

The suspension of the sentence is conditional on the unnamed fan not attending football stadiums for any official sports competitions for two years.

The individual has also been handed a fine along with "various disqualification penalties", Real Madrid said in a statement.

"This ruling adds to the criminal convictions already issued for racist insults against Real Madrid players at the Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas, and José Zorrilla stadiums," the club statement continued.

"Real Madrid, which has acted as a private prosecutor in this case and continues to do so in others involving similar incidents, reaffirms its commitment to combating racism and eradicating any racist behavior in football and sports."

The incident occurred during Real Madrid's 3-0 win over Real Oviedo at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium in August 2025, during which Mbappe bagged a brace.

Vinicius Jr , who has been persistently targeted with racist abuse at multiple stadiums in Spain as well as online, also scored in the match.

After the match, LaLiga reported alleged racist chanting towards Mbappe and Vinicius to Spain's National Police, with the league alleging that chants imitating monkey sounds were heard on multiple occasions.

In March 2024, Vinicius broke down in tears during an emotional press conference as he bemoaned that racism was getting worse as perpetrators were going unpunished.

"I just want to play football but it's hard to move forward… I feel less and less like playing (due to the racist abuse)," he said.

articles.title: 🏆 Louzán adamant: 2030 World Cup final can only be in Spain
articles.summary: Rafael Louzán, president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), has been unequivocal about the venue for the next World Cup final. Speaking on Tues...
articles.body:
Rafael Louzán , president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF ), has been unequivocal about the venue for the next World Cup final. Speaking on Tuesday at the Expansión & Marca Business Sport Forum in Madrid, he stated bluntly that "the 2030 World Cup final can only be held in Spain, and it will be held in Spain".

The head of Spanish football ruled Portugal out of the running to host the final, pointing out that the neighbouring country does not have a stadium with a capacity of 80,000. He also stressed the tournament's geographical identity in the face of Morocco's ambitions, emphasising that "this is a World Cup that belongs to the European continent".

However, Louzán issued a stark warning about Spain's administrative deadlines and institutional agility compared with its African rival. "The countdown has begun, and we need to move quickly to get everything ready and the work done in time. In Morocco, just one person is in charge, whereas here several people are in charge at government level", he warned those attending the forum.

The federation president therefore urged public authorities to "get to work" as soon as possible, saying the time had come to act to avoid falling behind on preparations.

Finally, Louzán revealed that he has already told FIFA of the need to settle the matter internally as soon as possible, rather than waiting until 2028, the date initially scheduled for the official announcement.

articles.title: Brazil legend Romario calls for manager Carlo Ancelotti to be sacked
articles.summary: Romario, Brazil's fourth-highest scorer behind only Neymar, Pele and Ronaldo publicly demands that legendary manager Ancelotti be relieved of his duties.
articles.body:
Few would have predicted that Carlo Ancelotti would be facing the wrath of a Brazil legend just 18 months into his tenure as head coach of the Brazil national team.

But Romario, Brazil's fourth-highest scorer behind only Neymar, Pele and Ronaldo, has publicly demanded that legendary manager Ancelotti be relieved of his duties not once but twice in the last week alone.

It all started after Brazil suffered a 3-2 friendly defeat by Japan on Friday thanks to a controversial stoppage-time winner from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto.

Ancelotti received a red card for dissent in the aftermath - the first of his international management career, as Barcelona forward Raphinha also saw red.

And in the wake of that defeat, despite it being a friendly, Romario quickly took to social media to air his frustrations about the former Real Madrid boss.

"Ancelotti, enough is enough! Pack your bags and leave!" he wrote on Instagram.

"Nobody questions your history. You are one of the greatest coaches world football has ever seen, but that was at club level."

Brazil were eliminated by Norway in the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, a result which ensured they failed to qualify for the quarter-finals for the first time since 1990.

And Romario alluded to this too, stating that the country "can't take the risk of throwing another World Cup in the trash - the time to act is now!"

The Brazil boss has been in the game long enough to know how to deal with all sorts of opinions.

He has won the Champions League a record five times as a head coach and won the league title in all of Europe's top five divisions, along with multiple domestic cups.

But his record with Brazil is far from perfect. Across 21 matches, they have recorded 12 wins, four draws and five defeats.

However, while Ancelotti acknowledges the need for improvement, he emphasised the fact that it is still "a new project."

Speaking before Brazil's friendly with Singapore on Tuesday the Italian said: "In a democratic country with freedom of speech, everyone is allowed to express their opinion.

"It's not up to me to say whether the things he says are correct, wrong or just stupid. The truth is that Romario talks a lot. A lot. It's his right."

Despite the criticism he has faced, Ancelotti feels Brazil are on the right track and who is to tell him otherwise when you look at his track record?

"I really like what we're doing," he said.

You would have thought that would have been enough to let it lie for the time being.

But before Brazil had even kicked a ball in their next friendly against Singapore, Romario was speaking out again.

The former striker, who is the ninth-highest goalscorer in football history with 784 goals, doubled down on his calls for Ancelotti to be sacked.

"I talk a lot because when it comes to the national team, I have size, weight and power of speech," Romario, 60, said.

"I do not speak to gain followers, I do not speak for people to like me. I speak my mind.

"I have worn this shirt for many years and I am pretty sure I was one of the ones that helped the little yellow be respected all over the world."

He said he respected Ancelotti but added he hadn't "added anything new" to the national side.

"We will find another coach who will do a better job than you. And I'm saying this to your face, not through a message, including to the president of the CBF, who is long overdue to fire you."

Brazil faced Singapore in their final match of 2026 on Tuesday and won 7-0 .

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior, who has come under scrutiny of his own so far this season, scored a hat-trick within the opening 21 minutes while Bournemouth winger Rayan and Chelsea's Estevao were also on the scoresheet.

It's a result that may bring a pause to proceedings in this war of words for now. However, if this last seven days has proved anything, it's that this saga is likely far from over.

articles.title: Piqué criticizes 12-game ban for Andorra goalkeeper after collision that led to player's death
articles.summary: MADRID (AP) — Andorra owner Gerard Piqué has questioned the 12-game ban handed to goalkeeper Jesús Owono following a collision that resulted in another playe...
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — Andorra owner Gerard Piqué has questioned the 12-game ban handed to goalkeeper Jesús Owono following a collision that resulted in another player's death, saying the punishment should have been based on the challenge rather than its tragic consequences.

Piqué, a former Spain and Barcelona defender, criticized the sanction in a video posted on TikTok late Monday, two weeks after Owono's on-field collision with 30-year-old Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel in a second-division match.

De Miguel, who was nicknamed "Demi", died the following morning.

Piqué said "there is no sanction that could give us Demi back," and noted that it will take more than 12 games for Owono to be ready to play again. But he didn't think the punishment was fair to the goalkeeper.

"I truly believe imposing the maximum suspension on Jesús for this challenge puts him in a position he doesn't deserve, because he is not to blame for everything that happened," Piqué said.

"What this sanction does is make it look like he was responsible for the consequences of what happened. The sanction should have been for his action, not for the consequences."

Piqué cited a challenge in another match that brought a three-game suspension, and recalled his own collision with Barcelona teammate Víctor Valdés in 2012. He said players, former players and coaches had described the Owono incident as an accident.

The disciplinary committee that punished Owono — who was sent off after the collision — said the goalkeeper used "excessive force."

De Miguel was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Owono, who rushed far outside his area, near the end of the Nov. 2 match in Tenerife. De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest following the collision.

Owono issued a statement through his club expressing his grief and offering his condolences to De Miguel's family.

Police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely.

Last week, Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again.

articles.title: David Beckham Sues After His Fragrance is Sold in Gas Stations and Discount Stores
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — A dispute over the sale of David Beckham perfumes has struck a sour note with the soccer star turned style icon.
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — A dispute over the sale of David Beckham perfumes has struck a sour note with the soccer star turned style icon.

Beckham's commercial company is suing a beauty firm after his "luxury" fragrances were allegedly found for sale in discount stores and a gas station bargain bin.

DB Ventures has filed a claim in the New York Supreme Court against German beauty group Coty, which makes and distributes a range of Beckham-branded fragrances and toiletries. They include the Classic and Instinct lines and the eaux de toilette Intimately and Exquisite Leather.

The claim argues that Beckham's "world-renowned global brand is synonymous with excellence and refinement," and "David Beckham products are a symbol of everyday luxury."

"Imagine, then, the shock and dismay experienced when DB Ventures discovered that David Beckham products were being offered for sale in a gas station," the legal document says. "How could this possibly have happened? Desperation and greed."

Lawyers for DB Ventures allege that Beckham-branded products "ended up in the bargain bin inside a gas station" and at British budget retailer Poundland, "allowing the product to be sold for dollar store prices and associating the David Beckham brand with cheap, discount products."

DB Ventures is seeking at least $41 million in damages for breach of its licensing agreement.

Coty has asked a judge to dismiss the lawsuit, which was filed in April. The company argues that New York courts have no jurisdiction in the case, and says DB Ventures is using the claim to "manufacture its early exit" from its licensing deal and hand over the Beckham contracts to another firm, Interparfums.

Coty and DB Ventures did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Tuesday.

Beckham, the former soccer star for Manchester United and Real Madrid and captain of the England men's national team, parlayed success on the pitch into a lucrative business career that includes co-ownership of soccer team Inter Miami. He was knighted last year by King Charles III, becoming Sir David.

He also has had a very public persona as a fashion model, "Bend it Like Beckham" movie muse and is husband to Spice Girl-turned-fashion designer Victoria "Posh Spice" Beckham. The couple have four children.

The Sunday Times Rich list earlier this year estimated the Beckhams' wealth at almost 1.2 billion pounds ($1.58 billion).

articles.title: UEFA Nations League Predictions, Including Wales vs Portugal
articles.summary: The UEFA Nations League matchday six continues on November 17, with eight fixtures, including Wales vs Portugal and Denmark vs Norway. Last Word on Football...
articles.body:
The UEFA Nations League matchday six continues on November 17, with eight fixtures, including Wales vs Portugal and Denmark vs Norway. Last Word on Football brings you our predictions for the final set of group games in the UEFA Nations League.

UEFA Nations League Matchday 6 Fixtures: November 17

Group D gets most of the attention on the final night of the UEFA Nations League group stage. Denmark vs Norway is first on our list. The Danes' confidence will be sky-high after their brilliant win over Portugal, which has put them in pole position to finish second in the group and qualify for the next phase. The Norwegians beat Wales last time out, and need to beat Denmark to reach the next round. This game could well be the game of the night.

Next up for us is group H, where Bosnia and Herzegovina hosts Romania. We believe the home side will do the job and end their group campaign on a high.

Prediction: Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 Romania

Back to Group D we go, and it's Wales vs Portugal this time. The Portuguese had looked impressive under Jorge Jesus, but were humbled 4-1 by Denmark last time out, and will be eager to end the group phase on a high.

In Group G, Ireland and Kosovo will battle it out for second place at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin. We are anticipating this one to be close, but the home advantage will be key here and will help Ireland secure second place in the group.

In Group F, Ukraine play Georgia, with both teams out of form; this should be a close, scrappy fixture. We are backing the Ukrainians to edge this one.

Also in Group F, first plays second, with Northern Ireland in the top spot travelling to Hungary, who lie just a point adrift. Northern Ireland are yet to concede a goal in the group stage and will be tough to break down.

Prediction: Hungary 0-0 Northern Ireland

In Group H, Poland hosts Sweden. Despite the Swedes already securing the top spot, we are struggling to see anything other than an away win here.

The final fixture for the UEFA Nations League group stages takes us back to Group G, where the winless Israelis host table-toppers Austria. The Austrians have the top spot secured, but they will want to seal their dominance with a win and preserve their unbeaten record.

The UEFA Nations League group stage is almost complete, and on the final night, attention will mostly be on Group D. Portugal will be focused on banishing the memory of their defeat to Denmark, and we see them brushing Wales aside. But the real drama in the group could come in the Denmark vs Norway game, with qualification on the line for both. It was 3-2 last time, and this could give us plenty of goals again.

Elsewhere, Ireland vs Kosovo is a big game for both nations, and we think home advantage will be massive in this one. Overall, not the deepest fixture for the final day of group stage fixtures, but enough still to play for.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel fee revealed! Real Madrid set to pay Manchester United nominal compensation for teenage sensation as contract details emerge
articles.summary: Real Madrid are on the verge of completing a sensational swoop for Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel as the financial details of the deal begin to emerge....
articles.body:
Real Madrid are on the verge of completing a sensational swoop for Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel as the financial details of the deal begin to emerge. The teenage sensation is expected to formalise his move to the Spanish capital within days, marking the end of a long-running transfer saga.

Madrid finalise three-year deal and €360,000 fee

Gabriel's new agent, Ali Barat, visited Valdebebas on Monday to iron out the final terms of the agreement, according to journalist Pablo Gallego . The 16-year-old is now expected to put pen to paper before the end of the week.

Per El Chiringuito TV reporter Marcos Benito, the English youngster will sign a three-year contract with Los Blancos . Real Madrid will pay Manchester United a nominal €360,000 fee in training compensation to secure his signature.

Behind the Old Trafford exit and rejected peace talks

The transfer follows a breakdown in Manchester that began when Gabriel walked away from the club in September . He has not trained with the Premier League giants since his departure.

Dissatisfied with United's plans for his first-team integration , the teenager asked the club to cancel his registration. The Red Devils rejected that request and later attempted to reconcile, only for their efforts to go unanswered by Gabriel and his camp.

Why the real cost dwarfs the nominal compensation

While the €360,000 compensation figure appears modest for one of England's brightest young talents, Real Madrid's total financial outlay will be far higher. Once the player's salary, agent fees, and commissions are factored in, the overall operation could cost between €10–15 million.

Securing the wonderkid also marks a major recruitment win for the Spanish club. Gabriel turned down serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, and Barcelona in order to make the move to Madrid.

Youth football first and a potential legal battle

Gabriel will join Real Madrid's Castilla setup upon signing, though federation rules prevent him from playing for the reserve team until January. He will feature for the club's youth sides until he becomes eligible.

Off the pitch, the saga may continue even after the deal is completed. Reports indicate that Manchester United could consider legal action against Gabriel, his representatives, and Real Madrid once the transfer goes through.

articles.title: Jurgen Klopp reveals he tried to sign Marc-Andre ter Stegen for Liverpool: ‘But he preferred Barcelona’
articles.summary: Having served as Barcelona’s first-choice goalkeeper for years, Marc-Andre ter Stegen faced a perennial battle with Manuel Neuer in the national team setup a...
articles.body:
Having served as Barcelona's first-choice goalkeeper for years, Marc-Andre ter Stegen faced a perennial battle with Manuel Neuer in the national team setup and never found himself well poised to be Germany's starting goalkeeper.

For years, the opportunity continually evaded him, to the point where it appeared he may well complete his career without enjoying the honour of being his country's starting goalkeeper.

Now, on loan at Ajax from Barcelona , he is finally enjoying his time as a regular starter for Germany and has been doing well for both club and country after what was a difficult period for him. Last night, he played all ninety minutes in their rout over Xavi's Netherlands.

Manager of the German national team, Jurgen Klopp, spoke to the media about the goalkeeper after his team's demolition of the Netherlands and heaped praise on Ter Stegen.

Klopp tried to sign Ter Stegen at Liverpool. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

In what came as a surprising development, he admitted to being interested in signing the Barcelona goalkeeper when he was the manager of Liverpool.

"I have always considered him an exceptional goalkeeper and I wanted to bring him to Liverpool, but he preferred Barcelona," he said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo .

Klopp then went on with his usual humour, stating that he did not have any hard feelings against Ter Stegen for rejecting his approach.

Slowly reviving his career. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

While Ter Stegen's loan at Ajax is only until 2027, Barcelona likely do not have him in their plans for the future.

Joan Garcia, after all, has established himself as the No. 1 starter in goal at Barça and Dominik Livakovic stands as a more than able deputy to the Spaniard.

The real purpose behind Barcelona loaning their former captain, quite clearly, was to help him make his name in Europe once more – something he has done well over the past few months.

Needless to say, their idea will be to part ways with him in the summer, possibly to make some profit and primarily to clear their wage bill given how finance remains one of their primary areas of concern.

articles.title: Carmona se fractura la tibia y el peroné en el entrenamiento: adiós a la temporada
articles.standfirst: El jugador sufrió la lesión en una acción fortuita durante la sesión de este martes
articles.summary: El jugador sufrió la lesión en una acción fortuita durante la sesión de este martes
articles.body: Los Servicios Médicos del Sevilla han informado de que José Ángel Carmona ha sufrido, durante el entrenamiento de este martes, una fractura de tibia y peroné de su pierna derecha durante una acción fortuita de la sesión. Tras el entrenamiento, el jugador fue trasladado a un centro hospitalario en el que se ha confirmado su diagnóstico y será sometido a una intervención quirúrgica. Los plazos de recuperación de este tipo de lesión suelen rondar los seis meses, por lo que Carmona podría haber dicho adiós a este temporada. "El Sevilla FC quiere trasladar un mensaje de ánimo a José Ángel, uno de los capitanes del club y canterano nervionense desde la categoría alevín. Asimismo quiere mostrar todo su apoyo durante su proceso de recuperación", se lee en el comunicado del club.

articles.title: Thomas Frank explains why Crystal Palace job was ‘too good to turn down’
articles.summary: Frank was appointed Palace manager after Pierre Sage’s sacking
articles.body:
Thomas Frank decided the Crystal Palace job was "too good to turn down" after talks with chairman Steve Parish.

The 53-year-old Dane, out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February, has spent the last nine months travelling, spending time with family, and reflecting on his career.

He takes charge of what he believes is an "iconic" English club , but one with plenty of work to do if they want to escape the Premier League relegation battle.

"You know, honestly speaking, I was a little bit, 'When do I want to go back in? Is it now?' Then this opportunity came up," Frank told PalaceTV.

"I was thinking, this is probably too good to turn down for various reasons."

Frank's strong admiration for Eagles supporters – he was at Wembley when Palace lifted the FA Cup – was a contributing factor.

He added: "The second part of it was the very good conversation with Steve Parish. He's been around, he knows what's happening, he knows how to run a football club.

"You always say you need to do your due diligence about the one who takes the decisions, and everything I've heard about Steve, everything I knew, it was positive, and then on top of that the conversation with Matt Hobbs, Iain Moody, was big.

"So all that adding up, looking into the team that I see is extremely exciting, good potential, or just thinking, 'Hmm, this is interesting'. And when I'm sitting here, walking around the training ground, it was just, 'Ok, you're back', which scared me a little bit, but it's good."

That Hobbs and Moody helped convince Frank to sign a two-and-a-half year deal will, for Palace fans, carry hope that the new boss will be backed in the January transfer window.

The Eagles lost a number of key personnel in the summer from their Conference League-winning squad, including Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea.

Their absence has been felt on a side that has conceded the most goals, 24, in the Premier League.

"To state the obvious, we need to stabilise things," said Frank, who pointed to defending, set pieces in both boxes, and defensive transitions as priorities to address, beginning with Saturday's trip to Coventry.

"We need to bring energy, we need to bring belief, we need to bring confidence, because this is a very, very good team with very good players, but they need to believe in themselves.

"We need to balance a lot of things with aiming high in Europe, two fantastic cup tournaments, but of course the Premier League is the most important if we need to prioritise, but we would like to compete in all things."

Frank, who was sacked by Tottenham after a run of only two wins in 17 matches, said he needed to "re-energise" after that disappointment.

He travelled to Japan and Australia with his family, spent a rare summer in Denmark, reflected on a relentless decade of work, and started speaking to people to get inspiration. Then, Palace called.

"Timing is everything in football," he added. "Coming back to the convincing conversation with Steve, Matt and Iain convinced me that this was the right time to come back."
